explicacion.en: English “I have” suggests tener, but the present perfect is built with haber: he viajado. Tengo means “I own / I possess”.
After he, has, ha, hemos, han you always need the participle (-ado or -ido), never the present form.
In Ecuador, a finished moment in the past (ayer, anoche) takes the preterite: viajé. The present perfect is for life experiences up to now: nunca he viajado.

titulo.en: Experiences up to today: haber + participle

texto.en: To say what you have or haven't done in your life, Spanish uses the present of haber plus a participle: he, has, ha, hemos, han + viajado. This is the same idea as English “I have traveled”. The participle never changes: he viajado, ha viajado, hemos viajado. Form it from the infinitive: -ar verbs end in -ado (viajar → viajado) and -er / -ir verbs end in -ido (comer → comido, vivir → vivido). Careful: haber is not tener. Say he viajado, never tengo viajado. In Spanish, haber and the participle stay together, so nunca goes before haber: nunca he comido cuy. Use the present perfect for experiences: ¿Has estado en Cuenca? Nunca he estado. For a finished moment, such as yesterday, use the preterite: ayer viajé. Ecuadorians use the present perfect less than people in Spain, but it is very natural with nunca, jamás and alguna vez. Pronunciation: the h is always silent, so he is “eh”, ha is “ah”, hemos is “EH-mohs” and han is “ahn”. The d in -ado is soft, like the th in “this”: viajado.

texto.en: Some very common verbs do not form the participle with -ado or -ido. Learn these eight: hacer → hecho, ver → visto, poner → puesto, volver → vuelto, escribir → escrito, abrir → abierto, decir → dicho, romper → roto. They work just like regular participles after haber: he hecho la reserva, hemos visto la habitación, he puesto el pasaporte en la mochila. After haber the participle never changes: he escrito dos correos, not he escritos. With estar the participle describes a state and it does agree with the noun: la ventana está abierta, la puerta está cerrada, la reserva está hecha. Pronunciation: in hecho and dicho the h is silent and ch is like the ch in “church”: “EH-cho”, “DEE-cho”. In roto the r at the start of a word is rolled.
Eight participles to memorize. Tap each word to hear it.

texto.en: Use ya to say that something is already done: ya he hecho la maleta (I have already packed). Use todavía no, or aún no, for something not done yet: todavía no he desayunado (I haven't had breakfast yet). Both usually go right before haber, and nothing comes between haber and the participle: todavía no he pagado. In answers you can use ya or todavía no alone: ¿Ya pagaste la cuenta? — Sí, ya. / Todavía no. In Ecuador people often use ya with the preterite for something finished: ya pagué la cuenta, ¿ya hiciste la maleta? The present perfect with ya and todavía no is also correct and very common when you are describing where things stand right now. Pronunciation: todavía is said “toh-dah-VEE-ah” and the d is soft, like the th in “this”.

titulo.en: Para and por: a first look

texto.en: English uses “for” in many ways, but Spanish splits it into para and por. In this class you learn four useful uses. Use para for a destination: un boleto para Baños, and for a purpose, with an infinitive: voy a Baños para descansar. Use por for a price, an amount of money exchanged: pagué ocho dólares por el boleto, veinte dólares por los dos. Use por also for a part of the day: por la mañana, por la tarde. Another useful phrase when you buy tickets is de ida y vuelta (round trip); solo de ida means one way. In Latin America boleto is the usual word for ticket. Pronunciation: the ll in ventanilla and llegada sounds like the y in “yes”.

objetivo.en: Understand signs with the infinitive (no fumar, prohibido estacionar, se ruega esperar) and solve a small travel problem.

nota.en: Singular in Spanish: el equipaje. The j is a strong h: “eh-kee-PAH-heh”.
Tiene un retraso = it is delayed.
The usual word in Ecuador and much of Latin America.

traduccion.en: excuse me (to someone you address as usted)

nota.en: Use it to get a clerk's attention politely.
Literally “it is requested”. Followed by an infinitive.

explicacion.en: English says “no smoking” with -ing, but a Spanish sign uses the infinitive: prohibido fumar.
A sign speaks to everyone, so it uses the infinitive, not a conjugated form: no estacionar.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Se ruega esperando en la fila.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Se ruega esperar en la fila.

explicacion.en: After se ruega use the infinitive: esperar, not esperando.
No fumas would mean “you don't smoke”. On a sign, use the infinitive: no fumar.

texto.en: Spanish signs and announcements usually use the infinitive, a short and impersonal form that speaks to everyone. No fumar means “no smoking”. Prohibido fumar means “smoking is prohibited”, and prohibido estacionar frente a la puerta means “no parking in front of the door”. To ask politely in a formal sign, Spanish uses se ruega + infinitive: se ruega esperar en la fila means “please wait in line”. You can add no: se ruega no dejar el equipaje solo. This se is the same impersonal se you already know: nobody in particular is asking. Finally, a typical travel question uses the present perfect and ya: ¿Ha llegado ya el bus? The answer is often todavía no: todavía no ha llegado. Pronunciation: in equipaje the j is a strong h, and in the infinitives fumar and estacionar the final r is a quick tap, like the tt in American “butter”.
Three phrases you will meet in the examples. Tap each phrase to hear it.

contexto.en: Sunday afternoon at the bus terminal in Baños. There are signs on the walls. Emma and Daniela wait for the bus to Quito. Emma and the clerk use usted.

dialogo.texto: Emma, ¿has visto el aviso? Dice: «Se ruega esperar en la fila».

traduccion.en: Emma, have you seen the sign? It says: “Please wait in line.”

dialogo.texto: Sí, pero no hay fila. Vamos a preguntar.

traduccion.en: Yes, but there is no line. Let's ask.

dialogo.texto: Disculpe, ¿ha llegado ya el bus de las cuatro?

traduccion.en: Excuse me, has the four o'clock bus arrived yet?

dialogo.texto: Todavía no. Tiene un retraso de veinte minutos.

traduccion.en: Not yet. It has a twenty-minute delay.
